Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

myutil 1.10.0

  • New upgrade_r_library(), run in a newly installed R to bring over the packages installed under an older one. For a patch upgrade (same x.y) it copies the package folders, so packages from GitHub, r-universe, R-Forge and local files come along without reinstalling; for a minor upgrade it reinstalls each package from where it came from. Packages the new R already has are left alone; translations and packages built under R < 4.0 are skipped; packages installed from local files are listed. With check = TRUE (default), the packages brought over are test-loaded in fresh R processes, in batches; dry_run = TRUE shows the plan.
  • New installed_pkg_sources(): classifies installed packages by where they came from (CRAN, another repository such as an r-universe, R-Forge, Bioconductor, GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket, local), from the Repository and Remote* fields in their DESCRIPTION.
  • New outdated_pkgs(): packages whose version on CRAN is newer than the installed one. old.packages() can flag hundreds of packages whose version hasn’t changed (e.g., right after an R upgrade), which update.packages() then reinstalls for nothing. Also shows the newest binary version and marks packages whose newer version is so far only available as source.
  • save_installed_pkgs() also saves pkginfo, the output of installed_pkg_sources(), and restore_installed_pkgs() uses it to reinstall each package from where it came from, skipping packages already installed. Files saved by earlier versions still work (CRAN only).
  • update_github() uses remotes::install_github(); it imported devtools::install_github(), although devtools is only suggested, which made R CMD check fail.
  • Fixes so that R CMD check is clean (0/0/0):
    • ls.objects() failed when there were no objects (as in a clean session); the example pattern = "*lm" was not a valid regular expression.
    • setwd()/cd() kept the previous directory in .lastdir in the user’s workspace; it is now kept inside the package.
    • dropbox_folder() no longer calls require(jsonlite) (it is imported).
    • Declared the utils functions used by Rpackages.bib(), update_pkgs() and use_data_doc(); .Rbuildignore covers the pkgdown files; Description is a sentence.

myutil 1.9.2

  • Rpackages.bib() gains add.pkg.doi = TRUE: fills in the CRAN package DOI (10.32614/CRAN.package.<pkg>) on a package’s own @Manual entry when its inst/CITATION omits it. Restricted to CRAN-installed packages, Manual entries recognizably about the package itself (not vignettes or other software), and entries with no existing DOI.

myutil 1.9.1

  • update_pkgs(): packages that stay out of date because this session has them loaded (e.g., cli, glue, rlang, vctrs) are now actually updated. The old retry ran a child process while this session still held their DLLs, so it always failed. Now a background R process, started through WMI so that it isn’t killed along with this session, waits for the session to exit, then installs them and appends the results to the same log.

myutil 1.9.0

  • First version with NEWS
  • Added reset_par() (2026-09-01: was defined without @export/docs since first added, so never actually usable as myutil::reset_par(); now exported and documented)
  • Added use_data_doc()
  • Added save_installed_pkgs() and restore_installed_pkgs(), for saving/reinstalling the set of installed packages across an R version upgrade
  • Added a CRAN release-check workflow, portable across packages: release_preflight(), release_document(), release_spelling(), release_spelling_add(), release_urls(), release_site(), release_build(), release_check(), release_check_win(), release_revdep(), release_cran_comments(), release_run_all()
  • Enabled markdown roxygen (Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE))
  • Reorganized README.md into categories
  • Added update_pkgs(), for non-interactive CRAN + Bioconductor package updates with logging and self-locked-DLL retry handling
  • Added Rpackages.bib(), for maintaining a master BibTeX file of R package citations. Dropped the old per-entry CRAN-DOI-stamping step – citation() already supplies the correct DOI (or none) per entry as of R 4.x, and the old step clobbered legitimate non-CRAN DOIs on Book/Article-type citations (e.g. citation("sf"))
